metric: Estimator disagreement, not ground-truth error or ATE.
time: Seconds from first input stereo frame, including initialization.
alignment: One initial yaw and translation; no scale/time/global trajectory fit.
quaternions: Schur Hamilton IMU-to-world; OpenVINS JPL world-to-IMU transposed.
limitations: Neither trajectory is ground truth; these differences cannot identify which estimator is correct.

Both use the same physical offline calibration and camera timestamps. Schur uses preprocessed IMU with original scalar noise; OpenVINS applies fixed matrices internally, so stochastic propagation is not identical.
Schur has no output before 10.975768 s on 003648; primary comparisons begin only when both estimates exist.
First sustained crossing means >=1 s uninterrupted, not a claim of monotonic divergence for the remaining recording.
OpenVINS online ablation changes only calib_imu_intrinsics with new calibration as initial values; it is not the earlier old-calibration online reference.
